issues.legal_issue: A landlord’s bona fide need to use premises for a proposed business may be established even if the landlord’s family members who will benefit from it lack expertise to operate the equipment, where qualified technicians or medical experts can be engaged.
A landlord’s choice of which premises to seek for a bona fide need cannot be dictated by a tenant merely because the landlord has other properties.
A compromise allowing a tenant to remain in specified premises does not bar later eviction proceedings unless it expressly and validly relinquishes the landlord’s right to seek eviction.
An earlier eviction decree based on a different need does not defeat a later claim of bona fide need, which is assessed as of the date the later eviction suit was filed.
